quest.title: A Gifted Rose: Ballad of Days Gone By
quest.description: Follow Sabbah's advice and try to "Awaken" the seeds
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Delicious Butter Chicken x1, Delicious Shawarma Wrap x2, Glabrous Beans x2

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Uncle Shafaqat. I wasn't able to fulfill your last wish...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Ah yes, you children were pestering me about the old ghost, weren't you? Well, that's not his real name. I mean, who would actually be called that?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I heard from my elders that his name was Shafaqat. He left Sumeru City when he was young and came to our village.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He built this house after arriving here and lived in it by himself, and for decades, he barely left.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've never seen him as a young man, but they say that he didn't really dislike children at that time.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He grew many trees and flowers in the front and back yard of his house. Children liked to run over to his place and ask for Ajilenakh Nuts, and also to listen to him talk.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: But by the time I met him, he'd already become old and was called the old ghost, and he'd also come to dislike children.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There must be another way.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: What other way can there be?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Uncle Shafaqat... That old geezer's already passed away in peace. If he was still alive, I could ask him what special methods could be used to cultivate these roses.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Who can I ask now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I know an Amurta researcher named Sabbah.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Oh, you mean that outsider girl. Can she help?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Besides, she came by here before and I drove her away. Will she still be willing to help?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll give it a shot.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: You're a good kid. It's alright if you can't find anyone to help. The thought is enough for me.

choices.text: Why are you so obsessed with growing flowers?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Once in a while, some outsiders would be forced to settle here in our village.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Some people never got used to living here, even if they kept pushing themselves to do so, and so they ended up alone for the rest of their lives.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: That old geezer Uncle Shafaqat was probably one of them. Everyone just accepted this state of affairs over time.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: But no matter how many years passed, I refused to get used to such a thing. It's really such a pity, what happened to him...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: You would have loved his garden too if you ever saw it. Pretty flowers of all kinds of colors, and so many trees of varying heights...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: The person who cultivated such a great garden passed away so quietly. And the only thing people would remember about him now is that the old ghost would take away naughty children.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I refuse to accept this. He wrote in his notes that he wanted these roses to grow everywhere. And I want to fulfill his wish.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I'm old anyway, so I don't care how others may see me. My life will be worth it if I can do this.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've cleaned up his house for him and sorted out the large pile of booklets he'd left behind.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I can show you a volume or two if you're interested.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I'll put these notes <color=#00E1FFFF>in front of the house</color>, just so he can see the sun for a bit through them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Affan...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Hmm? Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Sabbah about the difficulties Affan has encountered.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I see, so that's why you have come to me for help.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I'm honored that I am the one you thought of when something like this came up.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: That said, I did not specialize in plant cultivation, and my experience is limited. I'm not sure that I'll be of much help.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Still, I will try my best. The gentleman you mentioned who cultivated a new species of rose also interests me.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I will visit Mr. Affan's nursery when I have some time. You can look for me there later.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: This must be the person you found to help me, right? I said something harsh to her just a few days ago...

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I'm really... *sigh* I'm old and useless.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Aren't we having a friendly chat right now? Don't take it to heart, sir.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have the seeds germinated?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Mr. Affan and I went to take a look, and they haven't, unfortunately.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Based on my observations, these seeds appear to have gone through petrifaction. There are two possible reasons for this:

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: The first possibility is that they lost all possibility of growth after a long period of natural weathering and have thus transformed into a petrified state.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: If this is the case, the seeds will be unable to germinate. However, the probability of this hypothesis proving true is low.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It takes a very long time for petrifaction to take place, and these seeds do not meet that time requirement.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: The second possibility is that this breed has a strong affinity for Geo.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: That is to say that they can gather enough Geo elements while in seed form to form a stony shell over their exteriors.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: If the above hypothesis is true, this means that these seeds can be preserved for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon... Paimon doesn't really get it. Are you saying that the seeds have turned to stone?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: So they're stones, huh? Then I suppose all hope is lost. Golden Roses can't grow from stones.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Golden Rose? Do you refer to the Golden Rose that the folk song sings of?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Oh, you probably don't know about this. The village has a rose folk song that has been passed down, and it was originally composed by Uncle Shafaqat.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: He taught the folk song he composed to the generation before me, and they taught it to their own children.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: There are already people in my generation who have never heard of this song, and when our generation is gone, no one will remember him anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "Rose, oh roses, grant me my wish."

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "Blooming from the stone, the Golden Rose sang to me."

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: That's right... We can make the stones bloom!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you think of something, Sabbah?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: As the song hinted, perhaps breaking the stone shell will let the seeds sprout from the stones.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Normally, an ideal planting environment needs to be created to awaken the seeds and let them break through the seed casing on their own.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: But this rose breed has a seed casing that is too hard for the sprout to break through. So we can try lending them a hand instead.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Is this fine with you, Mr. Affan?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Do you mean to break the seeds open by force?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Obviously, we're not going to completely smash the seeds. We have to get someone nimble to do this.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, can you do it?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: You must be careful. Use <color=#00E1FFFF>Blunt Attacks</color> to break the seed casings first, then use the power of <color=#00E1FFFF>Dendro</color> to awaken the seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After you wait in silence for some time, young shoots slowly emerge from the soil...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Sabbah's method really worked!

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: They're finally sprouting! Finally...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Looks like Mr. Shafaqat's wish can finally be fulfilled after all.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Mr. Affan, you told me before that this breed of rose is something that he cultivated.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: To be able to cultivate a new species, he must have been a researcher who was exiled here, just like me, right?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Yes... He was exiled to this village, and he lived in the house behind us his whole life.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I see. That's probably how all of us exiles will end up.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, cultivating new species is something only the top researchers can do.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It's a great pity that a person like him faded into nameless obscurity so far away from the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you thinking about your own future as well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Keep your chin up.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Yes, child. You still have a long way to go, and lots of things to do.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Don't be trapped in melancholy. I don't want to see a second old ghost.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You're right. I shouldn't be getting all melancholic at a happy time like this. Let's get back on topic.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: These Golden Roses have only just sprouted. They have yet to bloom. I want to keep watching over them until they bloom. How about you all?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Same here.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Let's give them more time to absorb more nutrients. We'll reconvene later and watch them bloom.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "Rose, oh roses, grant me my wish."

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "Blooming from the stone, the Golden Rose sang to me."

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "She sang:"

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "No land but folk songs bore my spirit."

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "Songs shall defy my fate, and overcome my destiny."

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: "They will surpass me, surpass time. They will surpass the ever-lasting withering of life."

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: This is the song Uncle Shafaqat taught us.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Try using <color=#00E1FFFF>Blunt Attacks</color> to break the petrified seed casings, then use the power of <color=#00E1FFFF>Dendro</color> to awaken the seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a Sumeru Rose that I picked.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: How I miss this sight... Here, your presents are ready too. Please, take them.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: They're all seeds of plants that won't grow here. If you have a yard somewhere else, you can watch them mature there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Which Darshan were you with, by the way?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Oh, I could talk for three whole days about that!

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I was with Amurta and specialized in plant evolution, so you could say my work was evidence-based.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: That means it is impossible to reach new conclusions without new forms of evidence. Simply put, fossils are necessary for the study of historical plants.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: But there are only so many fossil samples available, and the Akademiya is limited in its ability to provide new ones.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Those were the circumstances, yet the institute still demanded results.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: So some people would just take a previous study, revise or add something to it, and turn it in. You also find that quite pointless, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: In truth, we could make new discoveries for sure if we looked towards history and geography for new materials.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Certain literary documents that Amurta would usually ignore could be used as well, though that would surely cross into Vahumana and Haravatat territory.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I was not proficient in those fields, and requesting the related files was too troublesome, never mind working with their researchers...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: But I believe that if we could actually work together as a team, many questions of the past would finally be answered.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It's a shame that we couldn't continue our collaboration attempts. I must say that people in Vahumana and Haravatat have very peculiar perspectives, though...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I had to be very careful with my wording and phrasing in my submissions to them to avoid misunderstandings and misinterpretations.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Before I was kicked out of the Akademiya, I was still in the middle of an argument with someone from Haravatat. Now I can't even do that...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Ah, I just rambled for a long time... But it feels good.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Before you got here, I really didn't have many friends, and it could get pretty lonely.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Very few people in the village are into gardening.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: ...Well, that's not entirely true. An old man living to the north of the village also plowed a plot to grow flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I've visited him before. He's a slightly eccentric old man.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I saw him planting stones, but he insisted that they were flowers, and even kicked me out.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It must be lonely, living all by himself. I can understand that.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You helped me with my Sumeru Roses... Maybe you can help him with his plants too.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You and Paimon should visit him if you get a chance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's life in Aaru Village?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It's alright. I have food and a roof over my head. All the essential things in life are taken care of.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I was banished, after all, so I can't dream of having books and research instruments here.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: This place has been used as exiled scholars' banishing grounds for quite a while. Life is hard and practical here, so naturally, no one here is interested in academics or research.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I'm certainly not the first exile, and probably won't be the last.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: All I can do is to learn to live with it.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Here for a chat? I've been wanting to talk to somebody.
